paragraphs: Hearing the narration of the intelligent Vi^wSmitra, Gautama’s eldest son, the exceedingly energetic S<it&nanda of rigid austerities, highly effulgent by virtue of his asceticism, with his down standing on end wondered greatly at the sight of Rama. And seeing the king’s sons seated at their ease, he said unto that foremost of ascetics, Vi^wamitra, — “O most powerful of anchorets, by thee was my illustrious mother, grown old in asceticism, shown unto the king’s son. Did my famous and exalted mother entertain with the produce of the woods Rama worthy of every one’s homage ? And, O highly energetic one, hath that old story relative to my mother having been wronged by that celestial, been communicated unto Rama ? And, O Kau^ka, good betide thee, hath my mother, in consequence of beholding Rama, been united with my revered sire ?

And, 0 son of Ku^ika, hath the highly energetic Rama come hither, after having been rendered homage by my highsouled revered sire ? And, O Kucika’s son, was my revered sire of quiescent soul, saluted by Rama when he arrived there ?” Hearing those words of his, the mighty ascetic Vi^wSmitra, skilled in speech, replied unto Satananda, cognizant of words, saying,— “O best of ascetics, nothing necessary w T as omitted by me, — but everything hath been done. And the ascetic’s wife hath been united with him, even as Renuka with Bhrigu’s son.*” Hearing the speech of the intelligent Vi^wamitra, the exceedingly energetic Satananda said unto Rama, — “Art thou well come, O chief of men ? It is by our luck that, O descendant of Raghu thou hast come unto us, headed by the respected Maharshi Vicw&mitra.

This highly energetic Vi^wSmitra, this Brahmarshi is of prowess measureless ; and deeds inconceivable, by virtue of his asceticism. Him thou knowest as r the prime >vay. O R&ma, there existeth on this earth not one that is more fortunate than thyself. Thy protector is even Kucika’s descendant, by whom mighty austerities have been performed. Do thou listen as I faithfully describe unto thee the ascetic pow f er of the high-souled Kau^ika. Do jzAmAyana. thou listen unto me relating this. This righteous one was for a long time a king, subduing his enemies, cognizant of morality, acomplished, and intent upon the welfare of his subjects. And there was a king named Ku£a, the son of PrajSpati. And Ku^’s son was the powerful and pious Ku9an£bha.

And Kuganabha's son was Gidhi. And Gadhi's son is the highly energetic and mighty ascetic Vi^wSmitra who ruled the earth. And that king reigned for thousands of years. And it came to pass that once with his four-fold forces marshalled, he set out for ranging the earth. And the king went on by turns ranging cities and kingdoms, rivers and mountains and asylums. And at length that foremost of conquerers, the mighty Visw&mitra, came upon Vasishtha's asylum furnished with various blossoming plants and trees ; abounding in animals ; inhabited by Siddhas and Ch&ranas*; graced by celestials and D&navas and Gandharbas and Kinnaras ; and filled with mild deer ; frequented by the feathered tribes ; crowded with Brahmarshis $ with Devarshis inhabiting it ; aye teeming with high-souled ones of accomplished ascetic success and resembling fire 5 like another region of Brahm£ ; graceful •> and adorned on all sides with high-soulded saints and V&lakhilyas and VaikhSnasas resembling Brahm&, feeding on water or air, or living on withered leaves, or subsisting on fruits and roots, and selfcontrolled, and free from faults, and of vanquished senses, and engaged in reciting mantras and performing homas.

verses.sa:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रस्य धीमतः।
हृष्टरोमा महातेजाः शतानन्दो महातपाः ॥

गौतमस्य सुतो ज्येष्ठस्तपसा द्योतितप्रभः।
रामसंदर्शनादेव परं विस्मयमागतः ॥

एतौ निषण्णौ सम्प्रेक्ष्य शतानन्दो नृपात्मजौ।
सुखासीनौ मुनिश्रेष्ठं विश्वामित्रमथाब्रवीत् ॥

अपि ते मुनिशार्दूल मम माता यशस्विनी।
दर्शिता राजपुत्राय तपोदीर्घमुपागता ॥

अपि रामे महातेजा मम माता यशस्विनी।
वन्यैरुपाहरत् पूजां पूजार्हे सर्वदेहिनाम् ॥

अपि रामाय कथितं यद् वृत्तं तत् पुरातनम्।
मम मातुर्महातेजो देवेन दुरनुष्ठितम् ॥

अपि कौशिक भद्रं ते गुरुणा मम संगता।
मम माता मुनिश्रेष्ठ रामसंदर्शनादितः ॥

अपि मे गुरुणा रामः पूजितः कुशिकात्मज।
इहागतो महातेजाः पूजां प्राप्य महात्मनः ॥

अपि शान्तेन मनसा गुरुर्मे कुशिकात्मज।
इहागतेन रामेण पूजितेनाभिवादितः ॥

तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः।
प्रत्युवाच शतानन्दं वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकोविदम् ॥

नातिक्रान्तं मुनिश्रेष्ठ यत्कर्तव्यं कृतं मया।
संगता मुनिना पत्नी भार्गवेणेव रेणुका ॥

तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य विश्वामित्रस्य धीमतः।
शतानन्दो महातेजा रामं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥

स्वागतं ते नरश्रेष्ठ दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि राघव।
विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य महर्षिमपराजितम् ॥

अचिन्त्यकर्मा तपसा ब्रह्मर्षिरमितप्रभः।
विश्वामित्रो महातेजा वेद्‍म्येनं परमां गतिम् ॥

नास्ति धन्यतरो राम त्वत्तोऽन्यो भुवि कश्चन।
गोप्ता कुशिकपुत्रस्ते येन तप्तं महत्तपः ॥

श्रूयतां चाभिधास्यामि कौशिकस्य महात्मनः।
यथाबलं यथातत्त्वं तन्मे निगदतः शृणु ॥

राजाऽऽसीदेष धर्मात्मा दीर्घकालमरिंदमः।
धर्मज्ञः कृतविद्यश्च प्रजानां च हिते रतः ॥

प्रजापतिसुतस्त्वासीत् कुशो नाम महीपतिः।
कुशस्य पुत्रो बलवान् कुशनाभः सुधार्मिकः ॥

कुशनाभसुतस्त्वासीद् गाधिरित्येव विश्रुतः।
गाधेः पुत्रो महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ॥

विश्वामित्रो महातेजाः पालयामास मेदिनीम्।
बहुवर्षसहस्राणि राजा राज्यमकारयत् ॥

कदाचित् तु महातेजा योजयित्वा वरूथिनीम्।
अक्षौहिणीपरिवृतः परिचक्राम मेदिनीम् ॥

नगराणि च राष्ट्राणि सरितश्च महागिरीन्।
आश्रमान् क्रमशो राजा विचरन्नाजगाम ह ॥

वसिष्ठस्याश्रमपदं नानापुष्पलताद्रुमम्।
नानामृगगणाकीर्णं सिद्धचारणसेवितम् ॥

देवदानवगन्धर्वैः किंनरैरुपशोभितम्।
प्रशान्तहरिणाकीर्णं द्विजसङ्घनिषेवितम् ॥

ब्रह्मर्षिगणसंकीर्णं देवर्षिगणसेवितम्।
तपश्चरणसंसिद्धैरग्निकल्पैर्महात्मभिः ॥

सततं संकुलं श्रीमद‍्ब्रह्मकल्पैर्महात्मभिः।
अब्भक्षैर्वायुभक्षैश्च शीर्णपर्णाशनैस्तथा ॥

फलमूलाशनैर्दान्तैर्जितदोषैर्जितेन्द्रियैः।
ऋषिभिर्वालखिल्यैश्च जपहोमपरायणैः ॥

अन्यैर्वैखानसैश्चैव समन्तादुपशोभितम्।
वसिष्ठस्याश्रमपदं ब्रह्मलोकमिवापरम्।
ददर्श जयतां श्रेष्ठो विश्वामित्रो महाबलः ॥
